answer: An identity exists only as a child: a parent spends one plume to endorse it and locks a glacier of frozen capital covering every ember it vouches for, and the child's ember must be at least that whole glacier. Each further child of one parent doubles the parent's lock, so a hundred clones of one operator cost more than a million times what one honest agent stakes, and the bill cannot be split. A newcomer under a fresh parent stakes one ember, the first honest price; spreading a fleet means hiring unrelated parents.
